cita: He et al. (2025). MADial-Bench: Towards Real-world Evaluation of Memory-Augmented Dialogue Generation.
problema: Existing memory-augmented-dialogue evaluation only tests PASSIVE recall (user explicitly mentions something) with query-oriented metrics (retrieval accuracy/perplexity), ignoring proactive recall triggered by emotional/situational cues -- important for emotional-support/companion use cases -- and lacking human-centred quality dimensions.
mecanismo: Not a memory mechanism -- MADial-Bench is a benchmark: a pre-built memory bank (171 memories / 160 dialogues / 1474 turns, Sec.3.1) grounded in cognitive-science two-stage recall theory, split into passive and proactive recall settings, with new scoring dimensions (memory-injection, ES-proficiency, intimacy) alongside standard retrieval-ranking metrics.
evaluacion: Task 1 (memory-recall, Sec.4.1): MAP/MRR/nDCG/Recall/Precision across 8 embedding models (Table 4). Task 2 (memory-recognition + generation, Sec.4.2): 3 settings (golden-only / golden+negatives / real-retrieval) across 8 LLMs, scored with BLEU/Rouge-L/BertScore plus human Likert ratings (naturalness, memory-injection, ES-proficiency, intimacy).
numeros_clave: Best embedding model (OpenAI text-embedding-3-large) does not exceed 60% Recall@1 / 62% Recall@10 on memory-recall (Sec.5.1, Table 4) -- a ceiling well below saturation even for the strongest retriever tested.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The strongest embedding retriever available (OpenAI-large) tops out under 60-62% Recall@1/@10 (Table 4) -- measured evidence that embeddings alone are NOT a solved retrieval problem, tempering any assumption that swapping in a better embedding model closes the gap for MF's own retrieval layer.

The passive-vs-proactive recall split (triggered by mention vs by emotional/situational state, Sec.2.1) is a useful vocabulary distinction for when MF's own memory should surface unsolicited vs on-demand.

notes: Table 4 (Sec.5.1, embedding-model recall ceiling); Sec.3.1 (benchmark construction scale).
